data.title: JPMorgan Sees US IPO Proceeds Near $290B In 2026, Says Investor Demand Is Growing Faster Than Supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan estimates IPOs raising $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation would carry a 1% to 1.2% weight in the Nasdaq-100 index.
  • Large IPOs can be considered for early inclusion in MSCI World indexes as soon as the 10th trading day, the firm said.
  • Private companies valued above $1 billion have reached a combined valuation of $8 trillion, JPMorgan said.

JPMorgan said Friday that the growing capital requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) companies are ushering in a new phase of financing in public equity markets, with U.S. IPO proceeds expected to reach $290 billion in 2026, approaching the 2021 peak of $330 billion.

In a note, J.P. Morgan Private Bank strategists said AI financing began with more than $700 billion in cash held by the largest technology companies. Alternative investors are expected to provide $1.4 trillion over the next five years, alongside $2.1 trillion in AI-related public corporate debt financing over the same period.

“The next level of financing is moving into one of the most traditional venues: the stock market. That means more equity issuance, and for some companies, an initial public offering (IPO),” it said.

The note comes a day after Anthropic (ANT) made its Nasdaq debut following the largest public offerings in history.

Investor Demand Is Growing Faster Than Supply

JPMorgan said the expected $290 billion in IPO proceeds represents less than 1% of the roughly $70 trillion U.S. stock market.

The bank noted that U.S. households purchased more than $800 billion in equities during the first half of 2026, while international investors added over $350 billion. Corporate buybacks have also exceeded $1.3 trillion year-to-date, providing another source of demand alongside cash-funded mergers and acquisitions.

“Overall, net equity supply has turned positive for the first time since the 2020–21 IPO boom, but demand – thanks to a multitude of factors – is growing even faster,” the JPMorgan note stated.

Index Inclusion Could Create Additional Demand

According to JPMorgan strategists, large companies entering public markets could attract another wave of demand through index inclusion, especially as the path to joining U.S. benchmarks has become smoother.

“A faster process can compress the timeline over which trillions of dollars in index-linked assets need to purchase shares,” they said.

JPMorgan noted that IPOs with a $100 billion raise and a $2 trillion valuation are estimated to have a 1% to 1.2% weight in the Nasdaq-100 and S&P Total Market Index. Meanwhile, in the MSCI World indexes, large IPOs can amount to a weight of roughly 10–11 basis points and be considered for early inclusion as soon as the 10th trading day.

Why Companies May Stay Private Longer

Despite the growing pipeline of large IPOs, JPMorgan said the case for remaining private longer remains intact. “For today's largest private companies, an IPO is increasingly about something different: creating liquidity and broadening access,” it said.

By the time these businesses go public, a meaningful amount of growth and value creation has already happened, the firm said, adding that it has just happened in the private market ecosystem rather than the public one.

It noted that private companies valued above $1 billion have reached a combined valuation of $8 trillion, while U.S. venture capital fundraising approached $110 billion through the third quarter of 2026.

JPMorgan said recent mega-IPOs suggest that public investors are “willing to pay a premium for companies that have become clear leaders in their markets.”

The rapid pace of technological advancements means some of AI's eventual winners may not yet exist, underscoring the value of patient capital and hands-on guidance in private markets, the firm said.

data.title: North Dakota oil producers moving crude by truck as pipeline outage continues
data.description:
North Dakota oil producers are moving crude by truck as a prolonged outage of Enbridge's pipeline in the state forces them to seek alternatives to avoid shutting in production.

"Some producers and marketers are trucking out production to delivery points on the Dakota Access Pipeline," Energy Aspects' head of global crude Jeremy Irwin told Bloomberg in an interview Friday. "Their tanks are filling up, and they can't get enough trucks to evacuate the Bakken crude they have, which could potentially lead to production shut-ins."

The North Dakota Pipeline, which delivers as much as 465K bbl/day of light, sweet crude to Canada and U.S. refineries, has been operating at lower rates since last week after a surge in reports of tainted crude forced Enbridge to implement testing for organic chlorides, slowing down the system.

It is unclear when the pipeline will resume normal production, and Energy Aspects said the source of the contamination must be identified and addressed before the system can fully restart.

Demand for Bakken alternatives from Canadian fields is increasing, reportedly prompting Enbridge to tell customers it will cut requested light crude shipments at Kerrobert, Saskatchewan, by 24% in December, the highest apportionment since February.

Marathon Petroleum's MPLX midstream arm reportedly issued a force majeure on North Dakota oil pipeline deliveries earlier this week.

data.title: Energy Empowering Foundation Secures Board Seat at NIP Group with 15.2% Stake
data.description:
Energy Empowering Foundation Secures Board Seat at NIP Group with 15.2% Stake

Energy Empowering Foundation, which owns Noveau Jumpstar Limited, disclosed beneficial ownership of a 15.2% stake in NIP Group Inc. The foundation reported that Noveau held 98,292,876 Class A shares as of November 13, 2026, after receiving shares in exchange for crypto-mining machines. Noveau also appointed Olga Sheng Jiang to NIP Group’s board, though the shares carry just 3.0% of the company’s total voting power.

Investor Intent

Noveau received 79,504,980 shares at the initial closing of a September agreement to sell crypto-mining machines to NIP Group. The agreement allows Noveau to receive additional shares at later closings and gives it registration rights and the right to appoint one director. Noveau used that right to appoint Jiang to NIP Group’s board by November 20, 2026.

Investor's Background

Energy Empowering Foundation is a Cayman Islands foundation company limited by guarantee and describes itself as a charity foundation. It owns all of Noveau Jumpstar Limited, an investment holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. Wu Weibin founded the foundation and serves as its sole director, with authority to direct its actions.

Original SEC Filing: NIP Group Inc. [ NIPG ] - SCHEDULE 13D - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down 11% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $86.56, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer to its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.13 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

-Emily Bary

data.title: Nymex Overview: Crude, Refined Products Lower as Supply Concerns Weigh — OPIS
data.description:
Crude futures moved lower with oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and recovering Middle Eastern production continuing to weigh on prices despite lingering concerns over regional conflict.

Both major benchmarks were on track for a third consecutive weekly decline.

January ICE Brent crude was trading 74cts lower at $91.24/bbl on Friday, while the February contract was down 67cts at $88.77/bbl.

December West Texas Intermediate slipped 46cts to $82.75/bbl, with January WTI off 43cts at $82.01/bbl.

Refined product futures were also lower. December ULSD fell 2.05cts to $3.9309/gal, with the January contract down 0.9ct at $3.8524/gal.

The December RBOB contract was trading 1.42cts lower at $2.4809/gal, with January down 1.12cts at $2.4580/gal.

Macquarie Group said resilient flows through the Strait remain a central factor for energy markets, including liquefied natural gas. Continued shipments through the waterway, alongside the persistence of the Iran blockade, could maintain pressure on oil prices, although the potential for further escalation in the region remains a risk, analysts said.

Recent U.S. Energy Information Administration data also point to improving regional supply. Oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints increased 19% in the third quarter from the previous three months, while regional crude production reached 23.1 million b/d in October, its highest level since the conflict began. EIA expects recovering Middle Eastern production and exports to contribute to rising global inventories, with relatively flat near-term demand.

data.title: Mexico likely to keep US aviation safety rating, airport operator says
data.description:
Mexico will likely hold onto the US Federal Aviation Administration's top aviation safety rating next year, the chief executive of Mexican airport operator OMA said, after recent concerns that the status could come under pressure.

  • OMA Chief Executive Ricardo Dueñas said in an interview on the Next Moves podcast, sent late Thursday, that communication between the Mexican and US authorities had improved in recent weeks and that the company was "very optimistic" Mexico would remain in Category 1 next year

  • Mexico regained Category 1 status in September 2023 after more than two years at Category 2, a downgrade that had barred Mexican carriers from launching new US routes and limited some code-share activity

  • The comments come after Mexican authorities said last month the FAA had flagged nearly two dozen issues to be addressed, prompting the government to boost the aviation regulator's budget and beef up staffing in an effort to strengthen oversight and avoid a downgrade

data.title: S&P 500, Dow on track for correction as Anthropic retreat weighs on AI stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 0.42%, S&P 500 off 1.88%, Nasdaq down 3.3%
  • Anthropic down 12.5% a day after debut
  • Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

The S&P 500 and the Dow were on track for a correction on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns.

Both benchmarks were down 10% from their record closing highs. An index falling 10% or more below its record high on a close-to-close basis is called a correction.

Anthropic shares tumbled 12.5% after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut.

The IPO, together with Nvidia's earnings this week, was seen as a key gauge of whether confidence in AI-linked stocks could recover after weeks of selling pressure due to concerns about elevated borrowing costs, regulatory uncertainty following Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections and the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

"Anthropic is so critical in assessing the overall market landscape in the end," said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth.

"You absolutely need to continue to see adoption and some form of price discovery as to what companies and individuals will be willing to pay for this technology ... until you get to a point where the market feels a little bit more confident that we've adequately priced it."

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed 8.6% to a seven-month low. Nvidia fell 7% to its lowest level since June 2025 and was heading for its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon was down 2% and Meta declined 3.6%, while Alphabet gained 1%. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped over 10% each.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors were lower, with the benchmark heading for its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The tech sector led losses with a 4.5% drop, while industrials and consumer discretionary slipped over 1.5% each.

Healthcare stocks were up 0.8% after four straight sessions of losses.

At 12:11 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 206.90 points, or 0.42%, to 48,890.16, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 135.15 points, or 1.88%, to 7,040.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 789.22 points, or 3.30%, to 23,091.82.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday said the US central bank's current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern."

Markets are pricing in a 98.2% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

A final University of Michigan survey showed consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0 in October.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 8.7% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.8-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 13 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 12 new highs and 626 new lows.

data.title: India cyber agency warns of unauthorised payment transactions
data.description:
India's cyber agency said on Friday it had reported unauthorised transactions at service providers for banking and financial services entities, and also at technology service providers supporting government-linked payments.

  • Payment fraud incidents extended beyond the financial sector to vendors and partner payout platforms, cyber agency CERT-In said in an advisory on Friday

  • Attackers altered business records or approval relationships and then used legitimate payment processes, it said. It did not say how much money had been improperly paid out, or by whom

  • The agency also said that it identified the use of AI-driven frameworks in cyberattacks across different sectors, and issued several recommendations for government organisations, non-financial payout platforms and technology service providers

  • India has seen a spate of cyberattacks on banks and non-bank lenders in recent weeks, even as ​authorities issued warnings and the Reserve Bank of India tightened cybersecurity checks

  • Earlier this month, CERT-In named the hacking group behind a wave of AI-driven attacks on financial firms and identified its tools, at least two of them linked to China

  • Late last month, India's central bank warned banks of rising cyberattacks on financial infrastructure, seeking proof of compliance with existing rules and details of their preparedness for ​AI-related risks

data.title: Apollo, Goldman lead $44 billion SpaceX GPU debt financing
data.description:
Apollo and Goldman Sachs said on Friday they priced about $44 billion of senior and subordinated notes to fund the purchase of GPUs and related equipment for SpaceX , in what the firms called the largest GPU financing to date.

The deal underscores the large capital requirements of the AI boom as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.

Here are more details:

  • The transaction, which was oversubscribed and upsized because of strong investor demand, is expected to finance the next generation of Nvidia Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout.

  • Lease schedules are expected to start when the GPUs and related equipment are delivered in the first half of 2027

  • BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and accounts advised by KKR provided anchor commitments

  • SpaceX said last month that an affiliate of Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the company in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion

data.title: European shares post worst week in over a year as AI trade unravels
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 logs weekly loss of more than 5% and closes at six-week low
  • Tech drops more than 5% as chip stocks sink
  • Vallourec slides after Q3 core profit decline
  • Cyclical sectors among major laggards

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Avinash P

European shares fell 2% on Friday and marked their steepest weekly decline since late March 2025, as investors unwound AI-linked bets after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut failed to revive confidence in the sector, deepening a selloff that spread beyond technology stocks.

The pan-European STOXX 600 closed down 2% to 625.65 points, logging a weekly loss of more than 5.7%, and registered its fifth straight session of declines. The index closed at a six-week low.

Anthropic reached a roughly $2 trillion valuation in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after a record IPO raise. But the shares dropped on Friday as the high-profile debut did little to ease concerns about the returns on massive AI spending.

Chip-linked stocks such as ASML and STMicroelectronics shed more than 9%, dragging the tech sector (.SX8P) down 5.4% in its steepest one-day fall since October 2025.

The AI trade that has underpinned a global equities rally in recent years came under pressure as investors questioned debt-fuelled spending, while political uncertainty in the US added to concern over the pace of the sector's expansion.

Investors also worried that a slowdown in AI-related spending could weigh on global economic growth, hurting sectors dependent on economic activity and business investment.

"The amplitude of the technology selloff is threatening the economic outlook and the latter is threatening probably the European cyclical stocks that are not necessarily benefiting from this technology selloff due to this reason, due to the impact that it is going to have on broader economic activity," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, a senior market analyst at Swissquote Bank.

Cyclical sectors including banks (.SX7E), defense (.SXPARO) and luxury (.STXLUXP) were among the other major laggards down over 2.5%.

"There's definitely a reassessment of AI and some nervousness around the trade," said Mark Preskett, senior portfolio manager at Morningstar Wealth in London. "Investors are sitting on good profits, so there's clearly some profit-taking. Multiples continue to fall for the hyperscalers and especially for semiconductor stocks."

Among other movers, Abivax plunged 17.2% after Scorpion Capital disclosed a short position in the French biotech firm.

Vallourec tumbled 14.6% after the French steel pipe maker reported a 26% drop in third-quarter core profit, citing the impact of the Iran conflict and operational disruptions in the US.

Despite this week's losses, the STOXX 600 is up 5.8% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500's roughly 3% gain and underscoring the resilience of European equities, which recently hit record highs on the back of stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings.

Consumer staples stocks outperformed, with Nestle , Unilever and British American Tobacco up more than 1% each as investors sought refuge in defensive sectors.

The circular in relation to the Scheme was published or made available to Eleco Shareholders on 2 October 2026 (the “Scheme Document”). Unless defined herein, defined terms shall have the meanings given to them in the Scheme Document.

As set out in the Rule 2.7 Announcement, Bidco had received a non-binding letter of intent from Raymond James Wealth Management Limited, trading as Charles Stanley (“Charles Stanley”) dated 8 September 2026 to exercise (or procure the exercise of) voting rights in favour of the resolutions relating to the Scheme and the Acquisition at the Meetings (or in the event that the Acquisition is implemented by an Offer, to accept or procure the acceptance of such Offer) in respect of 6,343,418 Eleco Shares, representing approximately 7.5 per cent. of the existing issued ordinary share capital of Eleco as at the last Business Day before the date of the Rule 2.7 Announcement (the “Charles Stanley Letter of Intent”).

Under the Charles Stanley Letter of Intent, Charles Stanley is permitted to sell, acquire or otherwise deal in Eleco Shares at any time.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 1 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 765,127 Eleco Shares in the period between the Rule 2.7 Announcement and 29 September 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 5 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had sold a total of 9,660 Eleco Shares on 30 September 2026 and 42,340 Eleco Shares on 1 October 2026.

As noted in the Update on Letter of Intent Announcement released by Bidco on 12 October 2026, Bidco became aware that Charles Stanley had transferred out 9,500 Eleco Shares from its discretionary holding on 6 October 2026 and sold 204,860 Eleco Shares on 8 October 2026.

data.title: US measles cases near 6,000 mark as outbreak worsens
data.description:
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday reported 5,838 measles cases as of November 19, as the country battles its worst outbreak of the viral infection in decades.

  • Measles cases in the US have climbed above 5,000 for the first time since 1991. Earlier this week, US lost its measles elimination status after 26 years

  • Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,589 measles cases, as of November 18

  • Wisconsin has reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated ‌death, involving a child

  • The CDC has confirmed six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not specify the states where the deaths were recorded

  • The gap in numbers follows a policy shift under U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., with the CDC switching to the National Center for Health Statistics' mortality data to track measles deaths, replacing its earlier reliance on state health departments' figures.

data.title: EU wheat pauses after four-week high as exports assessed
data.description:
Euronext wheat was little changed on Friday near a four-week high as fading hopes for a ceasefire in Russia's war with Ukraine supported EU export prospects while a steadier euro and a bumper Argentine harvest curbed price gains, traders said.

December wheat on Euronext was flat at €237.25 ($260.48) a metric ton at 1654 GMT. The front-month contract earlier rose to €239.25, its highest since October 21 and slightly above a previous four-week high set on Thursday.

March wheat , now the most-active position on Euronext, was up 0.2% at €233.50 a ton after touching a four-week peak at €235.25.

Russia launched one of the largest missile and drone attacks of the war on Ukraine on Friday, after President Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate for Ukrainian attacks on a bridge to Crimea.

This week's attacks and Putin's comments, in which he also rejected the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, have put the focus back on disruption to Black Sea grain trade, which has led to a surge in European Union exports.

In a sign of demand shifting towards the EU, Egypt agreed last month to purchase around 200,000 metric tons of Polish wheat and is discussing buying more, traders said this week.

"The Black Sea remains the focus," British merchant Frontier Agriculture said in a note.

But large Southern Hemisphere crop prospects could challenge EU exports, with Argentine wheat being offered at particularly low prices.

"Rain across Europe and the Black Sea is helping winter crops, and Argentina and Australia show no yield concerns, although quality is the risk if the weather turns," Frontier said.

Nearly all recently sown soft wheat crops in France were in good condition, data from farm office FranceAgriMer showed on Friday, suggesting showers this month have alleviated drought.

data.title: After Trump's China trip, US House Republicans push AI strategy to counter Beijing
data.description:
By Courtney Rozen

Two leading House Republicans on Friday urged US President Donald Trump to promote the development of lower-cost AI tools, according to a statement, arguing it would help US companies compete with increasingly popular Chinese alternatives.

House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino and House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar, both Republicans, made the appeal hours after Trump returned from meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. The president struck a notably warm tone toward China during the meeting. In contrast, the lawmakers warned that Beijing is using AI to make foreign companies dependent on Chinese technology, posing a threat to US economic and national security interests.

The lawmakers called on the Trump administration to give American companies developing what is known as open-weight AI models access to federal computing resources. Open-weight AI models are systems whose core components are publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific tasks. Reuters reported on Wednesday that the Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, a bid to discourage reliance on the technology without imposing ​new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing.

China leads in development of open-weight AI systems, which are gaining ground with US companies because they can be cheaper than AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic. They can also perform nearly as well. Chinese AI models were the three most popular by token usage in October on OpenRouter, an AI marketplace platform that tracks usage data. Tokens are units of data processed by AI models.

The lawmakers also urged the president to direct government agencies to use their products, arguing such steps would boost confidence in the technology among private-sector customers.

China and the US are competing for dominance in AI, with government officials in both countries arguing that leadership in the technology is critical to economic growth, military capabilities and national security. While Chinese companies have released a growing number of open-weight models, the US has lagged behind in the category. Some national security experts and industry advocates attribute China's gains in part to government support for domestic AI developers.

American-made open-weight offerings include Meta's Muse Glimmer, Nvidia's Nemotron and startup Thinking Machines' Inkling.

data.title: Trump officials met with hedge funds on Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern deal prospects, Bloomberg reports
data.description:
Officials from US President Donald Trump's administration met privately this week with hedge fund investors who were betting on the outcome of Union Pacific's proposed $72 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern , Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

The proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would create the first coast-to-coast freight railroad in the US. The proposed merger has raised concerns among freight shippers, labor unions and some state officials, who fear it could lead to higher rates and reduced competition.

The meeting included merger arbitrage investors and administration officials, who discussed the prospects for the rail merger, Bloomberg said, adding that officials did not share non-public information with attendees.

The White House, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern did not immediately reply to Reuters' requests for comment.

data.title: France, Germany to take key ECB roles, with Spain set for presidency
data.description:
Key points:
  • Spain likely to take presidency
  • Policy unlikely to change
  • High French debt among top risks

France nominated economist Laurence Boone to the ECB's executive board on Friday, as Europe's most powerful financial institution reshuffles three of the most vital roles in quick succession.

The European Central Bank is replacing its president, chief economist and the board member in charge of market operations, just as it fights high inflation and the prospect of renewed market turbulence triggered by French political turmoil.

Boone is expected to take on the markets portfolio. This could land the Santander executive and former OECD chief economist at the centre of any financial storm, particularly if it spreads beyond France and forces ECB intervention.

Friday's announcement puts Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos on track to take over from President Christine Lagarde in February while Germany's Markus Brunnermeier, nominated earlier this week, is likely to be the ECB's next chief economist when Ireland's Philip Lane leaves on May 31.

All nominations are subject to confirmation, which could still hit a snag as the reshuffle leaves the ECB's 27-member Governing Council with just one woman, since each of the euro zone's 21 national central banks is led by men and the board is also male-dominated.

Only one woman, Chrystalla Georghadji of Cyprus, has ever served as a euro zone national central bank governor and only five women have served on the ECB's board.

While the European Parliament cannot veto nominations, it has held back picks in the past in protest at the dearth of female candidates.

Nevertheless, the picks are likely to go through as Germany, France, Italy and Spain, the currency bloc's four largest nations, hold de facto permanent seats on the ECB board and negotiated for months over an acceptable package of nominations.

ECB watchers say that the new board is unlikely to change policy in the near term as inflation is now 4%, twice the rate of the bank's target, and continued policy tightening is the only appropriate response.

The real test could come if market tensions boil over.

France's debt level is the third highest in the euro zone and its budget deficit could be the highest this year as the French government is unable to push through meaningful reforms.

While the ECB has no mandate to prop up any single member, economists think it will come under pressure to act if contagion spreads to other countries or if the premium investors demand to hold French debt rises too high.
